<details open>

ggml : update CUDA/Metal radix Top-K to make tied selections deterministic (#31084)

* ggml : fix for the radix TOP_K thread timing bug

* make the key an ordered 64-bit pair

* a rewrite without shift-skip logic

* fix casts

* warp-contiguous layout

* reduce the scope removing vulkan+metal changes

* turn it off for Metal/ROCm, note about cub::DeviceTopK

* fix the hip build

* skip Vulkan as well

* popc lambda from fattn

* do block_cols math in int64_t

* make it allowlist bc SYCL looks non deterministic too

* ggml : make Metal radix Top-K tied selections deterministic

The radix top-k kernel gathered the selected indices with atomic
counters, so the order of the tied candidates at the threshold (and,
with more ties than remaining slots, the subset itself) depended on
the thread scheduling.

Replace the two atomic compaction loops with a deterministic scheme:
count the elements above and tied with the threshold in contiguous
per-thread chunks, rank them with a simdgroup scan and a serial scan
over the (now unused) radix histogram, and write each kept element
exactly once in column order. The output is now byte-identical
across runs.

This is also faster than the atomic version: the strided atomic
loops become contiguous passes, reducing top-k times by ~20-45% on
M5 Ultra, with tie-heavy shapes within a few percent.

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/GLM-5.3-Flash-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB)

Metal now produces deterministic tied selections for the radix top-k
path, so the determinism self-check runs for the MTL backend as well.

ggml-cuda : add d_state=64 fast path to SSM_SCAN kernel (#31818)

Zamba2 and similar architectures use a state size of 64 in their
recurrent-scan step, which fell outside the GPU kernel's existing
fast paths (96, 128, 256). Every scan step was falling back to CPU,
bottlenecking generation to 6-7 tok/s against the 50-70 tok/s band
other architectures achieve on the same hardware.

Add a 4th template instantiation for d_state=64, following the
existing pattern; no change to the underlying math. Verified against
the existing CPU-reference correctness harness with 3 new test cases
built from Zamba2's real hyperparameters (28/28 passing).

Measured ~35% throughput improvement (11 -> 15.1 tok/s) on Zamba2-7B-
Instruct. Full parity with other architectures not yet reached - a
separate, unrelated fraction of scan calls (~28%) still falls back to
CPU for a cause not yet diagnosed.

Assisted-by: Claude Sonnet 5

Co-authored-by: Sargentmajord <331229907+sargentmajord@users.noreply.github.com>

</details>
